title: Thinking Lab — STEM explainer animation channel on YouTube
soWhat: Turns textbook material in semiconductor physics, materials thermodynamics, crystallography, and materials characterization into English explainer animations of about 10–15 minutes each: equations are derived step by step, graphs build up alongside the narration, and every concept is tied back to real process and metrology settings such as solder, wafers, and SEM.
problem: Textbook derivations often skip steps and the figures are static, so it is hard to see how a curve responds when a parameter changes. Hand-edited animation is hard to produce at volume and consistently, and it is hard to guarantee that the numbers and equations on screen are correct.
role: Independently planned the topics, source textbooks, and series structure, and built a programmatic animation production pipeline (scripts and code written in collaboration with AI).
method: Animation is rendered frame by frame in code (Canvas 2D + MathJax equations, captured with headless Chrome and encoded with ffmpeg), so one engine produces every series
Numbers shown on screen are computed by Python numerical models and checked per episode, not typed in by hand
Sources include Neamen, Gaskell, OpenStax, and Zumdahl; every episode lists chapter timestamps and references
163 videos across 11 series so far: semiconductor physics, three seasons of materials thermodynamics, calculus, general chemistry, crystallography, materials characterization, and more

figures.caption: Materials thermodynamics: Pb–Sn free-energy curves and the common tangent explain why solder melts lowest at the eutectic point.
Semiconductor physics: charge, field, and potential of a pn junction derived together to get the depletion width.
Materials characterization: the SEM column and how working distance affects the image.
